decisionsResolvedAtSection277.title: Human assertion / regulatory predicates
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.section276Finding: A predicate clarification answer changed nothing. The panel is captioned "What would raise this" and offers Yes / No / Not sure; answering Yes left the candidate at the same confidence with the same missing predicate.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.decision: A generic review/confirmation action does not establish a previously unresolved regulatory fact. A regulatory predicate may become human-settled only when the user explicitly asserts the underlying fact, with provenance human_asserted. No silent predicate promotion.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.implementation: An explicit assertion channel keyed on the predicate the ENGINE named in its own clarification question, so the mechanism is general rather than another hand-maintained per-predicate table. Three limits hold it: only an UNKNOWN predicate may be settled (an assertion never overturns observed evidence), only a predicate the engine asked about can be settled (a generic confirmation carries no question id and cannot reach the code), and the settlement always carries provenance -- on the predicate, as an evidence fact under source `human_assertion`, and in the sentence the reviewer reads.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.verification: npm run test:hazlenz-human-assertion — 47 checks, 0 failures. Measured live: the candidate moves UNKNOWN 0.45 -> SUPPORTED 0.96 on an explicit "Yes", and stays UNKNOWN under every generic confirmation shape tried.

decisionsResolvedAtSection277.title: Low-confidence routing floor
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.section276Finding: On a deliberately safe observation -- a bench grinder correctly guarded, switched off and "isolated at the wall" -- the product proposed a ground_control hazard whose entire evidence was the single word "wall", routed at confidence 0.2 with no standard matched.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.decision: A candidate below 0.50 must not appear as a normal primary finding solely from weak semantic/lexical routing. Explicit governed deterministic evidence may route a hazard regardless of the semantic confidence. The threshold applies to routing/candidate generation, never as a universal rejection threshold for admitted Expert conclusions.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.implementation: A customer-visible candidate floor of 0.50 applied at the display boundary, so a below-floor route remains internal and is recorded in routingNotes rather than being dropped silently. The exception is the load-bearing half and was measured before it was written: ALMOST EVERY legitimate hazard routes at 0.2, so a bare threshold would have suppressed the §275 guarding case, the MSHA case and the fall-protection case. The discriminator is whether anything OTHER than the lexical router supports the candidate -- a governed standard candidate, or a whole-observation decision in the same family. Deterministic conclusions themselves are never touched.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.verification: npm run test:hazlenz-routing-floor — 26 checks including the known 0.2 "wall" case, 0.49/0.50/0.51 boundaries, and governed-evidence exemption. §117 remains 16/16 and the scoped-evidence suite 22/22.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.measuredConsequence: The floor also withholds a GENUINE hazard: the §276 electrical path -- a missing cover plate on a 480-volt disconnect with energised terminals exposed -- routes at 0.2 on the word "panel" and carries no standard, because the governed knowledge base has no electrical rule that fires on it. The product now reports that it did not establish a hazard rather than asserting one on a matched word, and the inspector's own "add a finding HazLenz missed" path remains. This is the rule working and exposing a real coverage gap in the knowledge base, and it is recorded as D-030 rather than absorbed.

decisionsResolvedAtSection277.title: Report revision / immutable issued artifacts
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.section276Finding: A renderer correction did not reach a report that had already been issued: the report fingerprint covered the inspection snapshot alone, so nothing about an unchanged inspection had moved. Separately, whenever the write path DID regenerate, it deleted the previous rows and destroyed their PDFs.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.decision: Issued reports are immutable artifacts. A correction creates a NEW revision with a new identity, timestamp and checksum, referencing the superseded report; the prior artifact is marked SUPERSEDED rather than deleted.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.implementation: The report fingerprint now covers the GENERATOR as well as the snapshot, so an authoritative renderer, severity or branding correction produces a new revision -- deliberately, when someone bumps GENERATOR_VERSION, not on every deploy. Superseded revisions are retained with status `superseded` and a pointer to the revision that replaced them, their artifacts are not retired, and they remain downloadable as the immutable record of what was issued. A later revision never rewrites an earlier one's supersession pointer. NO MIGRATION WAS REQUIRED: `superseded` was already in the status vocabulary and `supersededByVersionId` was already on the table; only the write path had not used them.
decisionsResolvedAtSection277.verification: npm run test:277-report-revision:db — 38 checks, 0 failures. Measured live on inspection #6: revision 2 (safety-insite-pdf/2) superseded by revision 3 (safety-insite-pdf/3), both downloadable, revision 2 byte-identical to its recorded checksum, revision 3 carrying the §276 severity-basis correction.

newDefectsAtSection277.defect: The governed knowledge base establishes no standard for an exposed-live-parts electrical condition, so after the D-024b floor a genuine electrical hazard is no longer proposed as a candidate.
newDefectsAtSection277.finding: Exposed by implementing D-024b, not caused by it: the hazard was previously surfaced on the lexical route "panel" alone, which is precisely what D-024b forbids. The correct remedy is a governed electrical rule, which is knowledge authoring rather than product scoping, and it is out of scope for a baseline-closure section.
newDefectsAtSection277.direction: Under-surfacing on a family with no governed rule. The inspector's own "add a finding HazLenz missed" path remains available and was verified present.
